descriptor.scene: There is no human being in this frame. EXACTLY TWO figures are in this picture and no others: the manager, and his tiny inspector. THE INSPECTOR IS NOT A SECOND MANAGER: he is BARE-HEADED with no cap and no hat of any kind, he is plainly smaller than the manager and plainly dimmer, and he never wears a newsboy cap. The camera is closer than an establishing view; the two figures fill the middle of the frame from the waist up and are the subject. At the LEFT, the manager, from the waist up, turned three-quarter, one mitten arm raised and extended toward the machine between them, head up. At the RIGHT and lower, standing on a small wooden step so he reaches the tray, the tiny inspector: the same small blocky luminous body, paler and dimmer, BARE-HEADED, holding up a small brass lamp with a warm amber flame in one mitten stub. Between and behind them the PAINT MACHINE: a rounded cream machine with an open tray at mitten height, and on the tray one freshly painted page lying flat, its wet warm colours catching the lamplight. The painted page shows a simple little painted interior whose window light falls clearly from one side. No lettering on the page. Behind them the factory falls away softly and out of focus; warm honeyed light, the manager's plum glow the strongest colour in the frame.
descriptor._caption: By the paint machine stands his smallest worker: an inspector with one job. The paint machine keeps putting the window light on the wrong side of the room, so after the third time, the manager posted him there. Now every painted page passes his little lamp before it moves on.
negatives: a cap, hat, newsboy cap or headwear of any kind on the inspector
the inspector the same size or the same brightness as the manager
a human being of any kind
readable text or lettering on the painted page
